summary.one_liner: Taxy AI is an open-source Chrome extension that uses GPT-4 (or GPT-3.5) to control your browser and carry out repetitive ad-hoc instructions on web pages.
summary.what_it_does: Taxy reads the current web page's DOM through a content script, strips it down to interactive or semantically important elements, and assigns each one an id. It sends this simplified DOM and the user's instruction to a selected LLM, which can respond with click(id) or setValue(id, text) actions. Taxy executes those actions through the chrome.debugger API and loops, adding each action to the history, until the LLM says the task is done, the user stops it, or an error halts it. Tasks are capped at 50 actions. The README says it currently supports only ad-hoc instructions, with saved and scheduled workflows planned for the future.
use_cases: automate repetitive actions in a web browser
schedule a calendar event with an AI agent
search and play a movie on a streaming site
fill in text fields on web pages using GPT-4
how_to_run: Run `yarn start` to build the package
In Chrome, go to chrome://extensions/, toggle Developer mode, click Load unpacked extension, and select the build folder
Open the popup with cmd+shift+y (mac) or ctrl+shift+y (windows/linux), or use the devtools panel, then paste an OpenAI API key
notable: Sends page contents and instructions only to the chosen LLM; the README says nothing is sent to Taxy's own servers
Simplifies and templatizes the DOM to reduce token count before each LLM call
Action cycle loop: observe DOM, ask LLM, execute one action, repeat, with full action history in each prompt
Safety-first design that halts automatically on unexpected LLM responses
Available as a popup or a devtools panel
caveats: Research preview; the README says many workflows fail or confuse the agent
Not on the Chrome Web Store; must be built and loaded locally from source
Requires the user's own OpenAI API key
